subject.title: fix(codex): stop stale MCP child processes with revalidated SIGKILL escalation

question: Is it acceptable for OpenClaw's Codex extension to force-kill a still-live Computer Use MCP child two seconds after SIGTERM when its command and ancestry still match?
rationale: The answer defines the supported lifecycle and failure semantics for a Codex-owned helper; tests can show mechanics but cannot establish whether abrupt termination is an acceptable product/runtime contract.

options.title: Approve bounded escalation
options.body: Confirm that matching stale Computer Use MCP helpers may be force-killed after the grace period, contingent on supported macOS app-server proof.

options.title: Keep graceful cleanup only
options.body: Retain SIGTERM-only handling and pursue a lifecycle fix in the owner path if a helper can legitimately ignore termination.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded escalation
recommendation.body: Confirm that matching stale Computer Use MCP helpers may be force-killed after the grace period, contingent on supported macOS app-server proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Most likely available routing candidate for the Codex app-server lifecycle contract based on recent related area work.
